## Purpose

This SOP describes the procedures for reserving, inspecting, operating,
and returning EA Program vehicles. Following these procedures ensures
that vehicles remain safe, reliable, and available for all program
research and teaching activities.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All use of EA Program vehicles for field research,
  class field trips, and program-related transportation
- **Does not apply to:** Personal vehicles used for commuting to field
  sites; rental vehicles; Facilities and Maintenance fleet vehicles
- **Location:** EA Program vehicle parking (campus garage)


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| EA Coordinator    | Manage reservation calendar, maintain insurance records |
| PI / Instructor   | Approve vehicle requests, ensure drivers are authorized |
| Authorized Driver | Follow this SOP, complete pre-trip and post-trip checks |
| New Students      | Submit insurance form and complete training before driving |


## Definitions

- **Authorized driver:** A person who holds a valid driver's license
  and has a completed, approved Pomona College driver insurance form
  on file with the EA Coordinator; the only persons permitted to
  operate EA Program vehicles.
- **Drowsy driving:** Operating a motor vehicle while significantly
  impaired by fatigue; a leading cause of serious crashes on long
  drives to remote field sites; if any crew member feels impaired by
  fatigue, pull over safely and rest before continuing.
- **Fuel card:** A fleet credit card stored in the center console of
  each EA vehicle; used to purchase regular unleaded gasoline (87
  octane) at participating stations; if declined, pay out of pocket
  and submit the receipt to the EA Coordinator for reimbursement.
- **Pre-trip inspection:** A walk-around check of the vehicle before
  departure to identify safety issues (warning lights, tire damage,
  fluid leaks) that would make the vehicle unsafe to drive; required
  before every trip.
- **Post-trip return standard:** The condition in which the vehicle
  must be returned after every use -- clean interior, at least 3/4
  tank of fuel, fuel card in the center console, no warning lights,
  parked in the designated garage spot.
- **Pomona College driver authorization:** The college insurance form
  required before driving any Pomona College-owned or -leased vehicle;
  submitted to the EA Coordinator with a copy of a valid driver's
  license; must be approved before the first trip.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Motor vehicle operation on public roads and unpaved
  field-site access roads; loading and unloading heavy field equipment.
- **Environmental:** Driving in adverse weather, reduced visibility, or
  on unfamiliar roads near field sites.
- **Fatigue:** Long drives to remote field sites increase the risk of
  drowsy driving.
:::

### Requirements

- Valid driver's license (must be carried while driving)
- Completed and approved Pomona College driver insurance form on file
  with the EA Coordinator
- Familiarity with this SOP and
  [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd)

### Emergency Procedures

In the event of an accident or breakdown:

1. Ensure all occupants are safe; move to a safe location if possible
2. Call 911 if anyone is injured
3. Contact Pomona College Campus Safety: (909) 621-8170
4. Notify the EA Coordinator and PI
5. Document the incident (photos, written description, other party
   information if applicable)
6. Do not admit fault at the scene; exchange insurance and contact
   information only
7. Complete a college incident report within 24 hours

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) for general
emergency response procedures.

## Procedure

### Before You Drive: Insurance Authorization

Before driving any EA vehicle for the first time, you must:

1. Obtain the Pomona College driver authorization and insurance form
   from the EA Coordinator.
2. Complete and submit the form with a copy of your valid driver's
   license.
3. Wait for written approval before operating any EA vehicle.

::: {.callout-important}
### No Exceptions
You may not drive an EA vehicle until your insurance form has been
approved and is on file with the EA Coordinator. This is a college
requirement, not a suggestion. Driving without approval puts you and
the program at serious liability risk.
:::

### Reserving a Vehicle

1. Contact the EA Coordinator to check availability.
2. Provide: date(s) and times needed, destination, number of
   passengers, and the name of the PI or instructor authorizing the
   trip.
3. Confirm the reservation before your trip; cancellations should be
   communicated as early as possible so others can use the vehicle.

### Pre-Trip Inspection

Before departing, walk around the vehicle and verify:

- [ ] Fuel gauge reads at least 3/4 full (refuel before departing if
      below 3/4; see §6.5)
- [ ] Fuel card is present in the center console
- [ ] Tires appear properly inflated with no visible damage
- [ ] All lights (headlights, brake lights, turn signals) are
      functional
- [ ] Mirrors are adjusted for the driver
- [ ] Windshield is clean and wipers are functional
- [ ] First aid kit is present and stocked (see
      [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd))
- [ ] No warning lights are illuminated on the dashboard
- [ ] Any pre-existing damage is noted and reported to the EA
      Coordinator before departing

If any safety issue is found (warning lights, tire damage, brake
problems), do not drive the vehicle. Contact the EA Coordinator
immediately.

### During the Trip

- Obey all state and local traffic laws at all times.
- All occupants must wear seatbelts (California law).
- The driver must not use a handheld cell phone while driving
  (California Vehicle Code §23123).
- Do not exceed the vehicle's passenger capacity.
- Secure all field equipment so it cannot shift during transport.
- On unpaved roads, reduce speed and increase following distance.
- If conditions become unsafe (severe weather, road hazards, driver
  fatigue), pull over and reassess before continuing.

### Refueling

1. Use the fuel card located in the center console.
2. Select regular unleaded gasoline (87 octane).
3. If the fuel card is declined or missing, pay out of pocket and
   submit the receipt to the EA Coordinator for reimbursement.
4. Replace the fuel card in the center console after refueling.

### Returning the Vehicle

After every trip, complete the following before leaving the vehicle:

1. **Refuel:** Return with at least a 3/4 tank of gas. If you used
   the vehicle, you are responsible for refueling.
2. **Clean:** Remove all personal items, trash, and field equipment.
   Brush or vacuum out dirt and mud. Wipe down surfaces if visibly
   soiled.
3. **Fuel card:** Confirm the fuel card is back in the center console.
4. **Park:** Return the vehicle to its designated spot in the campus
   garage.
5. **Report problems:** If anything is wrong with the vehicle (warning
   lights, unusual noises, damage, low tire pressure), notify the EA
   Coordinator immediately. Do not assume someone else will report it.

::: {.callout-warning}
### Return It Ready
The next person to use the vehicle should find it clean, fueled to at
least 3/4 tank, with the fuel card in the center console, parked in
the garage, and free of warning lights.
:::


## Prohibited Uses

- Personal errands unrelated to EA Program activities
- Transporting hazardous materials not approved by the PI (standard
  field samples and preserved water samples are acceptable)
- Allowing unauthorized or uninsured individuals to drive
- Off-road driving beyond established field-site access roads
- Towing trailers or other vehicles without prior approval from the
  EA Coordinator

## Training Record

Before driving EA Program vehicles independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd)
   in full
2. Submit a completed driver insurance authorization form to the EA
   Coordinator and receive written approval
3. Familiarize themselves with the vehicle (controls, mirrors, fuel
   card location) before the first trip
4. Be signed off by the PI or EA Coordinator
